function.name: compute_statistics
function.description: This function calculates key statistical measures, such as the mean, median, and mode, of a given dataset. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

data.description: An array of numerical values for which statistical measures will be computed.

include_variance.description: A flag indicating whether to include variance in the output. By default, variance is not included.

decimal_places.description: The number of decimal places to round the computed statistics to. The default is 2 decimal places.

message.content:
Sure! I’ll walk you through how to use our built‑in “calculator” (the **`compute_statistics`** function) so you can get quick answers on common math questions—mean, median, mode, and even variance when needed.

---

### 📊 What it does  
Given an **array of numbers**, this helper returns:

| Statistic | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Mean**  | Average value |
| **Median**| Middle value (or average of two middle ones) |
| **Mode**  | Most frequently occurring value(s) |
| **Variance** *(optional)* | Measure of spread |

All results are rounded to your chosen precision (default = 2 decimals).

---

### 🔧 How to call it  

```python
from functions import compute_statistics

result = compute_statistics(
    {
        # Your numeric data goes here:
        "data": [12, 15, 9, 10, 11, 14, 8],

        # Optional flags:
        "include_variance": True,
        "decimal_places": 1   # change as desired
    }
)

print(result)
```

#### Expected Output Format

```json
{
  "mean": 11.0,
  "median": 11,
  "mode": null,          // null means no single most frequent value
  "variance": 7.5       // only present because include_variance=True
}
```

> *If there’s more than one mode, the function will return all of them.*

---

### 🛠️ Quick Example – No Variance Needed

Suppose you have test scores `[88, 92, 75, 91, 85]`. You’d run:

```python
stats = compute_statistics({"data": [88, 92, 75, 91, 85], "include_variance": False})
print(stats)
```

Result:

```json
{"mean": 86.2, "median": 88, "mode": null}
```

*(Rounded to 2 decimals.)*
